name: CKS Kubelet, File & RBAC Hardening
description: Node-level CKS hardening you can't practice without real node access: control-plane manifest file permissions, kubelet readOnlyPort, apiserver NodeRestriction admission, least-privilege RBAC, Pod Security Admission, and a default-deny NetworkPolicy.
objective: CKS › Cluster + System Hardening. Prove you can harden file perms, the kubelet, apiserver admission (NodeRestriction), least-privilege RBAC, PSA, and network policy.

questions.title: Harden a static pod manifest's file permissions
questions.prompt:
A CIS benchmark finding: the kube-scheduler static pod manifest on the control-plane node `$CP` is world/group readable (it was left at mode `644`). The manifest files under `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/` should be owned `root:root` with permissions `0600` so non-root users on the node cannot read control-plane configuration.

Set the permissions of `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-scheduler.yaml` on `$CP` to exactly `600`.

_Hint:_ `docker exec $CP chmod 600 /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-scheduler.yaml`. Changing the manifest's mode does **not** restart the pod.

verification.description: kube-scheduler.yaml is mode 600 on the control-plane

questions.title: Disable the kubelet read-only port
questions.prompt:
The kubelet on worker `$W1` is serving its unauthenticated **read-only port** (`10255`). CIS requires it disabled. Edit `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml` on `$W1` so that `readOnlyPort: 0`, then restart the kubelet so the change takes effect. The node must stay `Ready`.

_Hint:_ `docker exec -it $W1 bash`, edit the file (set `readOnlyPort: 0`), then `systemctl restart kubelet`. Give the node ~20s to report Ready again.

verification.description: node $W1 is still Ready after the kubelet restart

questions.title: Enable the NodeRestriction admission plugin
questions.prompt:
Harden the API server so a compromised kubelet can only modify its **own** Node and Pod objects: add the `NodeRestriction` admission plugin to the kube-apiserver.

Edit the static pod manifest `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml` on `$CP` and ensure `--enable-admission-plugins` includes `NodeRestriction` (keep any existing plugins). The kubelet restarts the apiserver automatically; wait for it to come back.

_Hint:_ `docker exec -it $CP bash`, edit the manifest, add `NodeRestriction` to the comma-separated `--enable-admission-plugins` value (or add the flag if absent). A typo here takes the apiserver down, so edit carefully.

questions.title: Least-privilege RBAC for a read-only service account
questions.prompt:
In namespace `rbac-lab` there is a ServiceAccount named `reader`. Grant it **read-only** access to pods and nothing more: it must be able to `get` and `list` pods, but must **not** be able to `delete` pods (or do anything else).

Create a `Role` (in `rbac-lab`) granting `get`/`list` on `pods`, and a `RoleBinding` binding that Role to the `reader` ServiceAccount.

_Hint:_ `kubectl create role ... --verb=get,list --resource=pods -n rbac-lab` then `kubectl create rolebinding ... --role=... --serviceaccount=rbac-lab:reader -n rbac-lab`. Verify with `kubectl auth can-i list pods --as=system:serviceaccount:rbac-lab:reader -n rbac-lab`.

verification.description: reader SA CAN list pods in rbac-lab
reader SA CANNOT delete pods in rbac-lab

questions.title: Enforce the restricted Pod Security Standard on a namespace
questions.prompt:
Namespace `restricted-ns` must enforce the **restricted** Pod Security Standard via Pod Security Admission.

Add the label `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted` to the namespace, pinned to version `v1.29` with `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce-version=v1.29`.

_Hint:_ `kubectl label ns restricted-ns pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce-version=v1.29 --overwrite`.

verification.description: restricted-ns enforces the restricted PSA level, pinned to v1.29

questions.title: Default-deny NetworkPolicy
questions.prompt:
Namespace `netpol-lab` (which already has pods running) has no network isolation. Create a **default-deny-all** NetworkPolicy named `default-deny` in `netpol-lab` that selects **all** pods (empty `podSelector`) and denies **both** ingress and egress (it must list both `Ingress` and `Egress` in `policyTypes`, with no `ingress`/`egress` allow rules).

_Hint:_ a NetworkPolicy with `spec.podSelector: {}` and `spec.policyTypes: [Ingress, Egress]` and no rules denies all traffic to/from every pod in the namespace.

verification.description: default-deny policy selects all pods (empty podSelector) in netpol-lab
default-deny policy has both Ingress and Egress policyTypes
